title: Signal Harmonization and SLO Orchestration - 90 Day Campaign
content:
Context and why this matters:

This doc outlines a focused, 90-day cross-functional campaign to harmonize customer-facing signals (API latency, token-level tail latency, model-generation errors) into a small set of agreed SLIs and SLOs, build the automation and dashboards to measure them, and create a lightweight orchestration layer that teams can adopt for rollout gating. The intent is to reduce ambiguity during incidents, align product/infra priorities, and give Platform and Hosted teams a repeatable way to declare and defend availability targets for model serving paths.

Problem statement (observed pain):
- Multiple teams emit similar-but-incompatible latency metrics (api_ms_95, gen_ms_p95, nv_latency_p95) causing confusion in postmortems.
- No standard prefix-KV cache SLO for model warm-starts; customers see variance during burst traffic.
- Rollouts are blocked because feature owners and SREs disagree on “acceptable” degradation and rollback criteria.

Campaign goals (measurable):
1) Define and land a canonical SLI set for model-serving paths covering: request_accept_time, first_token_latency (FTL), end_to_end_95th, generation_error_rate.
2) Implement collection + cardinality normalization in the telemetry pipeline for top 6 services (hosted-api, dedicated-router, cache-manager, kv-store, model-worker, fallback-proxy).
3) Ship a shared SLO dashboard and an alerting guardrail matrix (canary, warm-up, full rollout) for 95th and 99th percentiles.
4) Run 2 cross-team rollout rehearsals using the gating automation; measure time-to-detect and mean-time-to-rollback/improve.

Success criteria (must be met within 90 days):
- 6 services emit the canonical SLIs to the metrics store with consistent units and tags.
- SRE + Product reach written agreement (confluence doc) on SLO targets for the hosting tier: p95 latency <= 220ms for small sequence, generation_error_rate <= 0.5% for production traffic.
- Canary automation prevents at least one harmful rollout during rehearsals and triggers rollback within 5 minutes.
- Post-campaign customer-impact reduction: at least 30% fewer customer-facing SLA-related postmortems attributed to metric confusion in prior quarter (measured by internal PM tracker).

Scope (what's in/out):
In: telemetry normalization (metric naming, tag schema), dashboards, alert rules, gating automation for canary A/B, training sessions and runbooks.
Out: full redesign of the serving runtime, deep model quality evaluation (beyond generation error rate), billing/reporting changes.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Campaign lead: Priya Raman (SRE lead) — overall coordination, roadmap steers, stakeholder sign-off.
- Product lead (Hosted API): Ava Thompson — SLO target negotiation, customer impact validation.
- Platform lead (Dedicated/Private): Miguel Santos — infra changes, capacity gating.
- Observability/Telemetry owner: Jordan Kim — metric schema, pipeline updates.
- Professional Services / Solutions Eng contact: Renée Laurent — customer playbooks and rollout comms.
- Engineering buddies: one eng contact from each service (TBD).

High-level timeline (90 days, by week ranges):
- Week 0 (kickoff + discovery): stakeholder map, inventory current SLIs, collect sample dashboards.
- Weeks 1–3 (definition + quick wins): draft canonical SLI schema, agree units and tag keys, ship metrics spec PR, start pipeline mapping.
- Weeks 4–6 (implementation phase 1): instrumentation changes for hosted-api and cache-manager (emit canonical SLIs), telemetry transform in metrics pipeline.
- Weeks 7–9 (implementation phase 2): instrumentation for model-worker and fallback-proxy, dashboard creation, and alert baseline.
- Weeks 10–12 (canary automation + rehearsal): integrate gating automation with CI/cd for two services, run rehearsals, refine runbooks.
- Week 13 (wrap + measurement): compile metrics, run retro, produce final guidance for adoption across org.

Workstreams and owner-level tasks (short checklist style):
1) SLI Schema and Naming (owner: Jordan Kim)
   - Draft metric names and tagging conventions
   - Publish spec PR and confluence page (linked_artifacts updated)
   - Create mapping script to convert legacy metric names during roll-out

2) Instrumentation changes (owners: service eng leads)
   - Add first_token_latency and generation_error_rate to request lifecycle traces
   - Ensure consistent percentiles (p50,p95,p99) via histogram buckets where possible
   - Validate tagging (region, deployment, model_variant, customer_tier)

3) Telemetry pipeline and cardinality control (owner: telemetry infra)
   - Low-latency transform to normalize incoming metrics
   - Cardinality rules to avoid explosion from model_variant tags
   - Test mode to mirror metrics to dev store before production flip

4) Dashboards and Alerting (owner: Observability PM)
   - Shared SLO dashboard with per-service/cross-service views
   - Alerting guardrails (severity, paging thresholds, suppression windows)
   - Automated SLO burn-rate alerts for canary windows

5) Canary gating automation (owner: Release Engineering)
   - Integrate with deployment pipeline to evaluate SLOs during canary window
   - Auto-rollback or auto-halt policies based on burn-rate and customer-impact heuristics
   - Expose a simple status endpoint for product owners to query canary health

6) Runbooks, training, comms (owner: Campaign lead + Solutions Eng)
   - Two 60-minute training sessions (SRE + Product) + quick reference cheat sheet
   - Incident playbook for SLO degradation that includes decision tree for rollback vs mitigation
   - Customer-facing communication templates for scheduled experiments and rollouts

Gating criteria (explicit):
- Canary window is a minimum of 15 minutes and must see at least 1% of expected traffic for the route or 1000 requests, whichever is larger.
- If p95 latency breach > 30% of SLO baseline OR generation_error_rate increases by 0.2 percentage points during the canary window, pipeline triggers a pause/rollback.
- Owners must provide a post-mortem within 72 hours for any canary that triggers rollback.

Instrumentation checklist (quick):
- Trace spans: request_received -> model_queue -> first_token_emitted -> request_complete
- Metrics exposed: request_count (counter), first_token_latency_ms (histogram), generation_error_count (counter), fallback_rate (counter)
- Tags: region, env, service, route, model_variant, customer_tier

Risk register (top items):
- Metric disagreement: different sampling/aggregation setups can produce inconsistent p95s. Mitigation: canonical histograms + mirrors to dev store for validation.
- Tag cardinality explosion: mitigated by model_variant bucketing and sampling.
- False positives during traffic spikes: include burn-rate checks and traffic-aware thresholds.

Rehearsal play:
- Rehearsal 1: Hosted API -> introduce a latency regression in controlled canary (non-customer tenants). Verify alerting and auto-halt triggers.
- Rehearsal 2: Dedicated route -> simulate cache-miss storms and validate warm-up SLO behavior and rollback path.

Communications plan:
- Weekly 30-minute sync (campaign standup) with stakeholders; notes in confluence page.
- Bi-weekly demo to eng-leadership showing dashboards + rehearsal outcomes.
- Pre-rollout announcement template (email + #release-notices) and post-event summary template.

Measurement and instrumentation for the campaign itself:
- Adoption metric: count of services emitting canonical SLIs (goal: 6).
- Time-to-detect: median time between SLO breach and alert firing across rehearsals (target < 2 min).
- Time-to-mitigation: median time from alert to rollback/halt (target < 5 min).

Open questions / decisions to be made in kick-off: 
- Should we include model-quality regressions (semantic failures) as SLO inputs now or in a follow-up?
- Exact SLO targets per customer_tier (prod vs dev) — product to propose defaults.
- Level of automation for rollback (manual-confirm vs auto), default to be conservative for high-risk routes.

Next immediate actions (first 7 days):
- Kickoff meeting invite + stakeholder alignment doc (owner: Priya)
- Jordan to publish SLI naming draft and open review thread (owner: Jordan)
- Patch list for hosted-api + cache-manager instrumentation (owners: respective leads)
- Telemetry infra to schedule mirror pipeline test and provide access to dev metrics store (owner: Miguel)

Appendix: short template for post-rehearsal notes (use in confluence):
- Rehearsal date/time
- Services included
- Traffic synthetic / sampled profile used
- Observed metric deltas (p50/p95/p99, error rate)
- Alerts triggered and timeline (first alert, action taken, rollback time)
- Lessons learned / next steps

Note: This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prioritizes landing a repeatable minimal instrument-and-guard workflow that product teams can adopt quickly. Expect iterative follow-ups that expand SLO categories (e.g., token-quality SLOs) after the 90-day campaign if adoption metrics are achieved.
